html:
The Battle of San Juan Hill was fought on 1 July 1898 on the heights east of Santiago de Cuba, in southeast Cuba. American troops stormed the Spanish positions that guarded the city.

It was the main land battle of the Spanish-American War. A Spanish fleet had taken shelter in Santiago harbour, and an American army under William Shafter landed nearby to take the city and force the fleet out. About 8,000 Americans attacked some 500 Spaniards dug in on the heights. The defenders' modern rifles caused heavy losses: more than 1,000 Americans were killed or wounded. Theodore Roosevelt and his volunteer Rough Riders took nearby Kettle Hill beside Black regular soldiers of the 9th and 10th Cavalry, who did much of the fighting and got little of the credit.

Two days later the Spanish fleet ran out of the harbour and was destroyed. Santiago surrendered on 17 July, and Spain asked for peace. It gave up Cuba and handed Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines to the United States. The battle made Roosevelt a national hero. He became president in 1901.
